questions.q: What problem does sharding solve that a replica set alone does not?
options: Write scaling and data sets larger than one server can hold
Read-only reporting queries
Automatic failover
Encryption at rest
questions.explain: A replica set gives availability and read scaling, but every member still holds the full data set — sharding partitions the data horizontally to scale writes and total capacity.

questions.q: What does mongos do in a sharded cluster?
options: Performs elections for replica set primaries
Holds the cluster's metadata about key ranges
Stores the actual document data
Acts as the query router applications connect to, routing operations to the correct shard(s)
questions.explain: Applications never talk to shards directly — they connect to mongos, which consults config servers and routes each operation.

options: User authentication credentials exclusively
A full copy of every document in the cluster
The cluster's metadata — which shard key ranges live on which shard
Only backup files
questions.explain: Config servers are a small replica set holding routing metadata that every mongos routing decision depends on.

questions.q: Why does a low-cardinality shard key (e.g. a status field with 3 values) cause problems?
options: It prevents mongos from starting
It can only ever be split into a few chunks, capping how far data can spread across shards
It causes immediate data loss
It has no effect on chunk distribution
questions.explain: With only a few distinct values, the data can't be divided into enough chunks to spread meaningfully across many shards.

questions.q: Why does a monotonically increasing shard key like an auto-incrementing _id create a hotspot, and what's the relational parallel?
options: Every new document's key is higher than the last, so all new writes land on the same shard — the same failure mode as a monotonically increasing partition key creating a hot partition
It has no relational parallel — this is a MongoDB-only problem
It causes the config servers to crash
It only affects read queries, not writes
questions.explain: New writes concentrate on whichever shard owns the highest key range, mirroring the classic hot-partition problem from bad relational partition key choices.
